description: Web attacks decomposed (OWASP top 10). SQL injection, XSS variants (stored, reflected, DOM-based), CSRF, SSRF, prototype pollution, deserialization, IDOR, security misconfiguration. The specific mechanisms by which web apps fail + the defenses.

sub_mechanisms.name: stored_XSS
sub_mechanisms.definition: Attacker payload stored in DB (comment, profile field); served to other users; executes in their browser.
sub_mechanisms.why: Worst XSS variant: persistent, affects all viewers. Mitigation: output encoding everywhere, CSP. Framework defaults (React JSX) escape automatically.

sub_mechanisms.name: reflected_XSS
sub_mechanisms.definition: Payload in URL or form input; server echoes back; executes in victim browser. Requires victim to click crafted URL.
sub_mechanisms.why: Phishing combined: malicious URL → page reflects script. Mitigation: encode URL params on output. CSP further limits damage.

sub_mechanisms.name: DOM_based_XSS
sub_mechanisms.definition: JavaScript code processes user input (URL fragment, location) and inserts into DOM unsafely.
sub_mechanisms.why: Server never sees payload; pure client-side. Mitigation: use safe DOM APIs (textContent, not innerHTML; setAttribute). Linters detect anti-patterns.

sub_mechanisms.name: SQL_injection_blind
sub_mechanisms.definition: Server doesn't echo results but behaviour differs based on injection. Time-based or boolean-based extraction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Slower than classic SQLi but recoverable. Tools (sqlmap) automate. Mitigation same as classic: parameterised queries always.

sub_mechanisms.name: SQL_injection_second_order
sub_mechanisms.definition: Input stored safely, but later used unsafely in different query. Triggers on second use.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tricky to find: input went through validation; output didn't. Mitigation: parameterise ALL queries, not just user-facing. Code review + SAST tools.

sub_mechanisms.name: CSRF_token
sub_mechanisms.definition: Random per-session value embedded in forms. Server verifies on submission.
sub_mechanisms.why: Classic CSRF mitigation. Modern alternative: SameSite cookies. Token approach still required when SameSite insufficient (cross-site flows).

sub_mechanisms.name: SameSite_cookie
sub_mechanisms.definition: Cookie attribute. SameSite=Lax: only sent on same-site navigation (default modern). Strict: same-site only. None: cross-site.
sub_mechanisms.why: Modern CSRF defense. Lax default in Chrome 80+, blocks most CSRF without token. Cost: must mark legitimate cross-site cookies (OAuth) as None+Secure.

sub_mechanisms.name: SSRF_cloud_metadata_attack
sub_mechanisms.definition: SSRF to fetch cloud instance metadata (169.254.169.254 on AWS). Reveals credentials, instance role.
sub_mechanisms.why: Capital One breach 2019: SSRF + cloud metadata = full data exfiltration. Mitigation: IMDSv2 (token-based metadata), block 169.254.* outbound from web services.

sub_mechanisms.name: IDOR
sub_mechanisms.definition: Insecure Direct Object Reference. /api/order/1234 — change 1234 to access other users' orders.
sub_mechanisms.why: Missing authorization check on object access. Common bug class. Mitigation: explicit authz check per object access, randomised IDs (UUIDs make guessing harder).

sub_mechanisms.name: prototype_pollution
sub_mechanisms.definition: JavaScript-specific. Modifying Object.prototype affects all objects. Often via deep-merge of attacker-controlled JSON.
sub_mechanisms.why: Used to escalate to RCE in some scenarios. Mitigation: use Map instead of plain objects, validate keys (no '__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype'), use Object.create(null).

sub_mechanisms.name: insecure_deserialization
sub_mechanisms.definition: Untrusted serialised data deserialised; may construct arbitrary objects with arbitrary state.
sub_mechanisms.why: Java + Python pickle famous for this. Mitigation: don't deserialise untrusted data; use safe formats (JSON for data only); add integrity check on serialised data.

sub_mechanisms.name: XSS_via_SVG
sub_mechanisms.definition: SVG files can contain JavaScript. Upload + serve as image → script execution.
sub_mechanisms.why: Image upload functionality often misses SVG. Mitigation: explicit SVG allowlist with strict sanitization, or block SVG, or serve as application/octet-stream.

derivation_rules.name: CSP_strict_nonce_blocks_most_XSS
if: site uses strict CSP with nonces
then: inline scripts without matching nonce blocked
derivation_rules.why: Even injected scripts can't execute without server-generated nonce. Stops most XSS in practice. Cost: must refactor inline scripts. Best modern XSS defense.

derivation_rules.name: parameterised_queries_complete_SQLi_fix
if: every SQL query uses bound parameters
derivation_rules.why: Parameters never interpreted as SQL syntax. Pure mechanical fix. ORMs help but raw SQL with concatenation defeats. Code review + linting catch.

derivation_rules.name: SameSite_Lax_blocks_most_CSRF
derivation_rules.why: Cross-site POST won't include cookies. Same-site navigation (link click) does. Covers ~95% of CSRF patterns. Edge cases require traditional tokens.

derivation_rules.name: IMDSv2_blocks_SSRF_metadata_theft
if: cloud uses IMDSv2 with mandatory tokens
then: SSRF can't fetch credentials via metadata
derivation_rules.why: v1: GET request fetches metadata. v2: requires PUT to get token first. SSRF typically only allows GET. AWS migrated, others followed. Direct mitigation for Capital-One-class attacks.

derivation_rules.name: framework_defaults_critical
if: framework auto-escapes by default (React, Vue, Django)
then: XSS is the exception, not the rule
derivation_rules.why: Pre-framework: every developer must remember to escape. Framework: must explicitly opt out (dangerouslySetInnerHTML). Statistical shift in vulnerability rates.
